headlines.title: Teen arrested in connection with deadly mass shooting at party near Morgan Hill
headlines.description: A 17-year-old was arrested on Thursday in connection with a deadly shooting at an unsanctioned party near Morgan Hill, the Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office said. The sheriff’s office said the 17-year-old suspect was taken into custody after authorities served a high-risk search warrant at a home in Salinas. He was arrested in connection with the mass shooting at an unsanctioned party in unincorporated Morgan Hill that left one person dead and injured six others on July 25, authorities said. More than 300 people were at the party, according to the sheriff’s office. Authorities said the suspect was identified after the community submitted numerous tips, videos and photos through the FBI’s digital media tip line.

headlines.title: Wrong-way crash on Montague Expressway in Santa Clara leaves 2 dead
headlines.description: Two men died Wednesday in a fiery, wrong-way crash on Montague Expressway in Santa Clara, according to police. Santa Clara police officers responded at about 11:58 a.m. to a reported crash on Montague Expressway at the Lafayette Street overpass and found two mangled vehicles, a GMC SUV on its side and fully engulfed in flames and a Honda pickup truck, police said. Citing a preliminary investigation, police said a man behind the wheel of the SUV was driving the wrong way on northbound Montague Expressway when he slammed into the pickup truck, which was being driven by a man. Both men died at the scene, police said. Their identities will be released by the Santa Clara County Office of the Medical Examiner. Police said the man driving the SUV may have been speeding, but his exact speed wasn’t immediately known. Chris Encizo said he was driving on Montague Expressway near the De La Cruz Boulevard intersection when the SUV driver suddenly started heading the wrong way and directly at him. Encizo said he narrowly missed a collision. “When I saw him, I got out of the way to the left side,” Encizo said. “He kept going. After 10 seconds, I see through my mirror that he crashed.” Encizo estimated the driver was going about 70 mph before the collision. Police said they won’t know if drugs or alcohol were a factor until toxicology tests come back. Anyone who witnessed the crash is encouraged to call Traffic Investigator S. Ernst at 408-615-4764. Those wishing to remain nameless are instructed to leave a message on the police department’s anonymous tip line at 408-615-4TIP (4847).

headlines.title: ICE arrests surge in Bay Area. Most appear to have no convictions or pending charges
headlines.description: ICE arrests soared to new highs across the country in July, with the surge in the Bay Area largely driven by the apprehension of immigrants with no known criminal convictions or pending charges, according to newly released ICE data obtained through a FOIA lawsuit by the Deportation Data Project. ICE documented roughly 49,000 arrests in July, the highest monthly total of President Trump’s second term, according to an NBC Bay Area analysis of the data. The data now includes the city where ICE recorded each arrest. In Bay Area cities, according to the data, the agency reported more than 330 arrests in July, a 76% jump from the same month last year. More than half of those arrests – about 189 – occurred in San Francisco. Immigration attorneys say they have seen many arrests occurring out of the public eye, including at ICE check-ins and immigration appointments. “That has been the trend in the Bay Area for the most part,” said Milli Atkinson, Director of the Immigrant Legal Defense Program for the San Francisco Bar Association. “People going voluntarily to their hearings, to their appointments, to their interview, and being detained at the 630 Sansome location in San Francisco or the location in Stockton.” Most of those arrested in San Francisco – about 83% – have no past criminal convictions or pending charges, according to the data. Atkinson said they’re seeing an uptick of arrests at airports and cautioned that anyone who is not a US citizen or lawful permanent resident could be a target. “Most of the arrests that we’ve seen at airports are people who at one point had a visa into the United States and that visa has expired,” Atkinson said. “But many of these people still have lawful presence in the United States. They have a work permit. They have an application pending.” ICE said it does not comment on the Deportation Data Project’s findings as it cannot “verify the source of, accuracy, completeness, or methodology of the data.” “The bottom line is that the Deportation Data Project is not accurate,” the agency said in a statement. The Deportation Data Project says on its website the records were produced by ICE in response to a FOIA lawsuit. ICE added that nearly 70% of ICE arrests are of “illegal aliens charged or convicted of a crime in the U.S.,” but did not provide supporting data or specify what time period it was referring to.
headlines.source: Hilda Gutierrez, Michael Bott and Lucia Walinchus

headlines.title: 49ers vs. Raiders live updates: San Francisco closes preseason with 18-12 win
headlines.description: What to Know The San Francisco 49ers (2-1) eked out an 18-12 win over the Las Vegas Raiders (1-2) in their 2026 NFL preseason finale on Thursday night at Allegiant Stadium. Eddy Piñeiro was perhaps the star of the game, connecting on all six of his field-goal attempts on a night when he was one of just a few 49ers starters to play. Several young 49ers skill players had nice games, notably Jordan James, who had nine total touches for 55 yards. Jordan Watkins also impressed as a focal part of the offense, gaining 91 yards on seven touches. Mac Jones struggled in his two drives of action, going just 1-of-5 passing for seven yards. The 49ers gained only one first down with Jones in the game. Adrian Martinez couldn’t find the end zone in relief of Jones, but he did just enough to get the 49ers into field-goal range several times, which proved to be enough. Tatum Bethune had a strong day at the helm of the 49ers’ backup defense, recording 10 tackles and a first-half interception off a tipped pass by Fernando Mendoza. Rookie linebacker Jaden Dugger caught the attention of 49ers legend Patrick Willis with his play, recording 10 tackles and a near-sack of Mendoza. Read below for all the game highlights, news, analysis and postgame press conferences from Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas:

headlines.title: Police shootout at San Jose home leaves family with big cleanup bill
headlines.description: A San Jose family says they have been hit with a big cleanup bill after a deadly shootout between police and a suspect inside their home on Tuesday. The family says they’re deeply grateful for the police efforts to save them but were not expected to have the multi-thousand-dollar bill to clean up the aftermath. On Tuesday, San Jose police rushed in to confront a known violent criminal hiding at a home. There was shootout inside the home that left a sergeant injured and a suspect dead, but the immediate danger was resolved. The family living in the home was left shaken but grateful. However, mixed in with the gratitude was dread because bills for the damage done needed to be paid and, for now, that falls to the family. “I am incredibly grateful for the officer who risked his life to save the lives of my family and my grandkids but, wow. The house is major, major damage,” homeowner Brett Bymaster said. One bill came immediately. Bymaster paid $3,375 for biohazard cleanup. Desperate for help softening the financial blow, the family reached out to Mayor Matt Mahan, who said the city will help and will reexamine the reimbursement claim process. “As you can imagine this is not a very frequent incident, thankfully, but we will cover the cost of the biohazard cleanup and reimburse this homeowner for that, and that’s something our city manager will take care of. And then, I’m working with the city manager and the city attorney to look at the claims process more broadly,” Mahan said. Bymaster was very grateful but still faces thousands of dollars in structural repairs and a city claims process that usually takes about 45 days just for a decision. “Coming up with the funds for all those repairs… Pretty worried about that. Pretty concerned as a family how we’re going to get through that, you know, on top of finding enough money to have a place to stay, and the mortgage is still due,” he said. The family is still getting estimates on the cost for city and home insurance claims. Meanwhile, the Victim Assistance program of the District Attorney’s Office called and also offered to help.

headlines.title: Oakland stabbing spree suspect has lengthy criminal history, records show
headlines.description: Oakland police on Thursday identified a man suspected of stabbing five people, one of whom died, in an apparent series of random attacks earlier in the week. Jose Jesus Rodriguez, 34, was arrested Monday and booked into Santa Rita Jail on suspicion of murder, attempted murder and assault with a deadly weapon, among other alleged crimes. Rodriguez’s alleged stabbing spree began just before 7:30 p.m. Monday, when he is believed to have attacked 58-year-old Gonsalo Lopez at Cesar Chavez Park on 38th Avenue in East Oakland, according to police. Lopez died at the scene. Lopez was a chef in Alameda and his family said he often brough food and helped the unhoused in the park he was attacked. Oakland Aug 25 Oakland Aug 25 Oakland 10 hours ago Four more people — two men and two women aged 30s to 50s — were found with stab wounds that evening. “So far, we do believe that they were random, we don’t have any connection with the suspect and the victims, but it’s still early on in the investigation,” Oakland Police Capt. Gloria Beltran said at a news conference Tuesday. After officers responded to the first stabbing, a second victim was located near 38th Avenue and San Leandro Street, police said. While tending to that victim, another call came in reporting a third stabbing victim who had been found near the Fruitvale BART station. Two more stabbing victims were then found near 39th Avenue and International Boulevard. Officers located the suspect with the community’s help in the 1500 block of 39th Avenue about 30 minutes later. Three victims were all in stable condition Tuesday and one was listed in critical condition, according to police. Meanwhile, documents show Rodriguez has a lengthy criminal history, including a prior conviction for a 2019 stabbing spree. Police said in that case he stabbed an Uber driver and a garbage collector. Rodriguez was eventually released on parole, but court records show he racked up repeated parole violations. Some of Rodriguez’s violations include an arrest in June of last year for assault and violating a criminal protective order. Last October, police said Rodriguez bit someone and threatened that person with a knife. During that arrest, police said Rodriguez headbutted and tried to bite an officer. Court records also show Rodriguez used a wooden board “like an axe” to injure two women. The recent stabbing spree and criminal history has some asking why Rodriguez was still out in the streets. Former prosecutor and legal analyst Michael Cardoza said parole violations can result in additional jail time, but notes the system has some big flaws. “This is an example of how our system has swung a little bit too far about letting people out of jail and not holding them responsible for what they do,” Cardoza said. “When you have people like this, our judicial system isn’t able to cope with him and it ends up like this. So don’t look and blame judges — look at our legislators who put the laws in that hamstring judges.” Alameda County District Attorney Ursula Jones Dickson called the stabbing spree a “senseless act of violence.” “It’s sad that he had to take a life before the system actually dealt with him as he should’ve been dealt with a long time ago,” Cardoza said. Rodriguez is scheduled for an arraignment Friday morning in Alameda County Superior Court in Oakland. His bail amount wasn’t listed in court records Thursday. Anyone with information, video, or photos related to the case is asked to contact the OPD Homicide Section at 510-238-3821, or the department’s tip line at 510-238-7950, or can email footage to cidvideos@oaklandca.gov. Bay City News contributed to this report.

headlines.title: De Anza College program to fuel Tesla's next engineering technicians
headlines.description: A South Bay college and Tesla are teaming up to train the company’s incoming engineering technicians. The new program at De Anza College in Cupertino gives students the hands-on experience needed to support Tesla’s test engineering, research and development, and manufacturing departments. NBC Bay Area business and tech reporter Scott Budman takes a closer look at the program and examines how it is helping those building our future. Watch his report in the video above. headlines.title: Chevron refinery in Richmond poses higher cancer risk, new report says
headlines.description: A preliminary health assessment from the Bay Area Air District released this week found that residents living near the Chevron refinery in Richmond face a higher risk of cancer and other diseases. If the results of the assessment are confirmed, Chevron will have to implement a plan to reduce the health risks or install pollution controls at the refinery. The Bay Area Air District is the agency responsible for protecting the air quality in the region. In 2017, the district adopted a new rule that said facilities that could pose high health impacts will be subject to a preliminary health assessment to quantify the potential health risks. The air district identified the Chevron refinery as one such facility and hence commissioned the preliminary health assessment. Experts from the agency then conducted multiple studies and collected samples between 2017 and 2025 to prepare the assessment, which was released Tuesday. The assessment estimated that the refinery poses a maximum cancer risk of 37 in a million, which means that 37 additional people out of a million could develop cancer over a lifetime of exposure to the air pollution caused by the refinery. This is more than the district’s threshold of 10 in a million, beyond which facilities must implement a plan to reduce the health risk, according to a news release from the agency. Risk of other non-cancer disease from short-term exposure was also found to be beyond the district’s threshold. The report states that most of the cancer risk is due to benzo[a]pyrene, a pollutant that escapes through small leaks at pipe fittings and storage tanks, while the short-term health risks are mostly because of benzene from the refinery’s wastewater treatment system. The district is now requesting public input and will modify the risk estimates based on the community’s comments. “These findings give the Richmond community clear, science-based information about the health risks from refinery air pollution emissions,” Philip Fine, executive officer of the Bay Area Air District, said in the news release. “Community input is essential before we finalize this assessment because the people who live closest to the refinery have the most at stake.” If the results of the preliminary health assessment hold after reviewing public comments, Chevron will be required to implement a plan to reduce pollution, or to install best available pollution control, the district’s news release said. “The Air District’s own analysis acknowledges that the assumptions driving most of its cancer-risk estimate may overstate actual refinery emissions,” said Ross Allen, a spokesperson for Chevron. “We agree and have already found that the assessment includes equipment that is no longer operating and assumptions that do not reflect actual refinery conditions. These issues need to be resolved before this preliminary estimate is treated as an accurate model of community health risk,” Allen added. In June 2025, the district reached an agreement with Chevron on a new air pollution monitoring system at the Richmond refinery to better monitor hydrogen sulfide, a smelly and potentially dangerous gas. Chevron also agreed to pay a fine of $100,000 for insufficient monitoring of the chemical at the time. Then, in December 2025, the district slapped a fine of $900,000 on Chevron after the company failed to make upgrades to its pollution monitoring systems as mandated by a district audit. Responding to Tuesday’s preliminary health assessment, Richmond Mayor Eduardo Martinez said in a separate news release that the report provides a quantitative basis for preexisting public sentiment. “As a city, we will do everything within our power and ability to ensure that any corporation operating within our city limits does so with environmental and social responsibility,” he said. The Bay Area Air District will hold a community meeting to explain the report’s findings and the procedure for submitting public comment on Sept. 21 at 5:30 p.m. at the Richmond Memorial Auditorium & Convention Center. Community members can send in public comments on this issue until Nov. 23.

headlines.title: Napa man charged for allegedly starting 2025 Pickett Fire
headlines.description: Prosecutors on Thursday announced the filing of criminal charges against a Napa man for allegedly starting the Pickett Fire in August 2025. The Napa County District Attorney’s Office on Wednesday charged Juan Luis Gutierrez Marfil, 45, with felony recklessly causing a fire of a structure or forest, alleging that Marfil started the Pickett Fire in the 2300 block of Pickett Road in north Calistoga on Aug. 21, 2025. Marfil’s charges also have a special allegation that the offense caused more than $6 million in property damage, prosecutors said. According to Cal Fire, the Pickett Fire burned 6,820 acres, taking fire units 17 days to contain. Though no civilian or firefighter deaths or injuries were reported, the fire destroyed a single-family residence and four outbuildings. The home that burned was found within the perimeter of the blaze but was believed to be abandoned due to its remote location and lack of access routes, Cal Fire officials said. The Napa County Agricultural Commissioner’s Office estimated in November that the fire caused over $56 million in agricultural losses to winegrape vineyards and other crops. An arraignment hearing is set for Marfil on Sept. 9 in Napa County Superior Court.

headlines.title: Apple to lay off 147 employees from South Bay offices
headlines.description: Apple is laying off 147 employees – most of them software engineers – from its offices in Sunnyvale and Cupertino. The news came down on the same day Apple announced its next product launch event on Sept. 9 at its Cupertino headquarters. The company is expected to unveil new iPhones and Apple Watches. Apple CEO Tim Cook plans to step down Sept 1. Longtime Apple executive John Ternus will take over.

headlines.title: San Pedro Social reportedly closing after late-night permit denial
headlines.description: Another business in San Jose’s San Pedro Square is closing up shop. A co-owner of San Pedro Social says the venue will close following a vote earlier this week by San Jose leaders denying the business’ request for a late-night permit. The venue wanted to stay open until 2 a.m., according to The Mercury News. Council members reportedly cited multiple fights outside the venue as a reason for denying the permit. The reported closure comes on the heels of news that another business in the city’s popular entertainment district is slated to close. Last month, Sushi Confidential announced it would close its San Pedro Square restaurant to focus on its other South Bay locations. Sushi Confidential’s last day in San Pedro Square is Monday.

headlines.title: Fremont police search for hotel sexual assault suspect
headlines.description: Fremont police are asking for the public’s help finding a person of interest in an alleged sex assault at a hotel last week. Police officials didn’t say at which hotel the alleged assault took place but said it happened on Aug. 16 at 1:30 p.m. in the 40000 block of Lakeview Boulevard. The person of interest is described as a man with a medium complexion who is 40 to 50 years old and tall and thin, police said. His hair is dark with some gray, mid-neck to shoulder length and fell below his ears. He has light brown or green eyes and may have a mole or bump on the bridge of his nose. Police did not specify his race. The man is being sought for questioning and no charges have been filed at this time. Anyone with information about this case can contact Fremont Police Department’s Crimes Against Persons unit at 510-790-6900.
